mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in a month but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% in a month but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: when housing starts (HOUST) are above the 12-month moving average, it indicates strong demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST is above its 12-month moving average but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases simultaneously over a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in a month but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a shift towards accommodative policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during economic expansions (GDPC1 > 2% YoY), an increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month when GDPC1 > 2% YoY
failure_condition: If GDPC1 > 2% YoY and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in a month but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of those instances.
